directorStatement.audienceFeeling: Keen feels tiny in open water, then funny and capable for a moment, then frightened when the storm removes his map, and finally relieved when he chooses to follow Squeaky.
directorStatement.whoseScene: Keen’s scene, with Squeaky as the visible companion who first plays beside him and later gives him a direction to follow.
directorStatement.emotionalChange: Keen moves from performed confidence, to comic uncertainty, to panic, to a small steadying breath, to trusting Squeaky’s lead.
directorStatement.theLaugh: Keen confidently names Squeaky and then treats an upside-down map as enough information to be going in “one of the directions.”
directorStatement.visualSurprise: The friendly open water turns into a storm fast enough to swallow the horizon and snatch the map away.
directorStatement.carryForward: Keen is still in rough weather, without the map, following Squeaky through the storm.

shots.purpose: Make the empty sea feel enormous, turn Squeaky into Keen's first companion, then let Keen's confident map-reading reveal that he has no idea where he is going.
shots.performanceAssignment: Shot 1: the small sailboat travels left-to-right across endless blue water. Keen performs confidence while making quick balance corrections. Squeaky surfaces at screen-right, keeps pace, and chatters; Keen greets him, listens, names him, and the friendship lands in one shared look. Shot 2: without resetting the boat or screen direction, Squeaky makes one playful leap while Keen laughs and lifts the map from the boat. Keen checks the map, looks over the bow, checks it again, rotates it upside down, then peeks over its edge and completes the directions joke. The boat keeps travelling throughout.
shots.camera: Open wide with the boat small against endless water, starboard side and left-to-right travel. Push to a warm medium two-shot for the naming beat. Cut on Squeaky's leap to a medium on Keen, then push toward the upside-down map while Squeaky remains readable at screen-right. Preserve the same boat, travel axis, sail, cargo and open-water light.
shots.openingPose: Keen stands center-left in the boat with one hand lightly on the tiller and the other beginning to lift; Squeaky is just below the surface at screen-right with ripples rising where the next pop-up will happen.
shots.dialogueBinding: Keen speaks all four lines in order; Squeaky answers only with dolphin chatter and never forms human words.

continuityConstraints.value: Keen wears exactly two inherited aged-gold open cuffs with blank settings, one on each wrist. No crystals, aquamarine stones or glow. The cuffs never vanish, duplicate, swap wrists or change form.

continuityConstraints.label: Boat cargo state

continuityConstraints.label: Sailing physics

shots.purpose: Let the storm dismantle Keen's performed control in one escalating cause-and-effect run, ending with the map gone and Keen finally admitting that he is lost.
shots.performanceAssignment: Shot 1: continue from the upside-down-map landing. A hard gust loads the sail, the boat heels and rocks, and Keen slides, grabs the mast and yelps. The light falls, rain builds from drops to sheets, and Squeaky dives below the rough water and disappears. Shot 2: Keen tries to steer with one hand and clamp the map with the other. A stronger gust visibly catches the map and tears it from his fingers; he reaches and calls after it. Shot 3: match Keen's reach as the boat drops beneath him. His hand closes on empty rain; the map vanishes into the grey. He regains his feet, sees that the horizon has gone, lets the loss register, and admits that he is lost.
shots.camera: Begin medium on Keen, map and sail from the established starboard side. Jolt with the first heel, then widen to reveal darkening sky, rough water and Squeaky's disappearance. Track the stolen map toward screen-right, cut at maximum reach, and tighten slowly on Keen only after the map and horizon have both disappeared.
shots.openingPose: Keen stands center-left with both hands on the upside-down map at chest height, knees flexed; the sail is just beginning to pull hard from an incoming gust at screen-right, and Squeaky is still visible near the waterline.
shots.cutInMotivation: The slight dimming at the end of the map joke becomes the incoming gust; the cut lands on the sail beginning to pull hard.
shots.dialogueBinding: Keen speaks all three lines; Squeaky remains wordless and exits underwater.

shots.purpose: Turn Keen's fear into a small act of self-regulation, then let Squeaky's return give him a choice: accept help and steer toward trust.
shots.performanceAssignment: Shot 1: continue with Keen alone in the same storm. A distant lightning flicker makes him grip the boat edge. His shoulders show quick breaths; he closes his eyes, takes one slower breath, repeats his brave phrase, and settles only slightly. Shot 2: Squeaky's offscreen clicking makes Keen open his eyes and turn before Squeaky appears. Squeaky leaps beside the hull, dives, resurfaces farther ahead and repeatedly indicates a clear screen-right route. Keen questions him, studies the water, meets Squeaky's eyeline, decides, and nods. Shot 3: Keen answers with growing resolve, braces his feet and hauls the tiller. The bow pivots under water resistance and the sail remains wind-loaded as the boat follows Squeaky rather than sliding sideways.
shots.camera: Ride the established starboard-side boat motion in a steadier medium close while Keen breathes. Let Squeaky's chatter bridge into a pan toward screen-right, then widen to show Squeaky leading and the bow physically turning after him. End with both characters' motivated eyelines and a readable forward route through the storm.
shots.openingPose: Keen stands frozen at center of the boat with arms lowered and fingers beginning to curl upward toward the edge as distant lightning starts to flicker behind the rain.
shots.cutInMotivation: Reaction continuation from Keen’s frozen admission; the next visible change is the lightning flicker and his hands moving to grip the boat.

promptContract.prompt:
[Opening Stage]
Create a playable 16:9 opening for 4.B1.S1; frame-one anticipation, not portrait or payoff.

[References]
- Project-stable slots: @图1=Keen; @图2=Squeaky; @图3=prop:keen_sailboat; @图4=prop:keen_sailboat_departure_state; @图5=scene plate. Never swap roles.
- Multi-angle collapse: @图1=one Keen; @图2=one Squeaky; views are angles, not extra characters.
- @图1: Keen's complete, uncropped 360 turnaround is the 100% identity authority. Match Keen exactly as the same character shown in the turnaround. Preserve every visible feature and proportion. Ignore background and static pose; do not describe, redesign, simplify, beautify or reinterpret it.
- @图2: Squeaky's complete, uncropped 360 turnaround is the 100% identity authority. Match Squeaky exactly as the same character shown in the turnaround. Preserve every visible feature and proportion. Ignore background and static pose; do not describe, redesign, simplify, beautify or reinterpret it.
- @图3 is the exact keen sailboat prop authority; inherit design, material, construction and scale only; ignore its background and labels.
- @图4 is the exact keen sailboat departure state prop authority; inherit design, material, construction and scale only; ignore its background and labels.
- @图5 is the locked Scene Look plate; inherit world, viewpoint, scale, materials, light and atmosphere only.
- Keep Keen and Squeaky distinct; never blend or swap traits.

[Characters In Frame]
- Keen

[Intended Read]
Keen and the little sailboat feel tiny against a huge open sea; the frame leaves a friendly, expectant pocket at screen-right where Squeaky is about to surface, turning loneliness into first companionship without starting the later acting beat too early.

[Canonical Style]
Feature-quality stylized 3D CGI. Plush character materials with subsurface scattering; soft fur with individual strands catching the light; glossy eyes with bright catchlights; translucent wing membranes where light passes through. Warm amber key light with cool blue fill and a soft rim light; teal-orange cinematic grade. Shallow depth of field with soft bokeh, gentle ambient occlusion, subtle film grain. Appealing exaggerated proportions, large expressive eyes, soft rounded features. Emotionally warm atmosphere.

[Geography]
Starboard side of the little sailboat is visible; bow points screen-right and the boat travels left-to-right.
The boat sits low center-left in frame with the open sea extending far ahead to screen-right.
Keen stands inside the boat center-left, oriented toward the screen-right water and travel direction.
Squeaky is just below the surface at screen-right beside the moving hull, indicated by rising ripples in the waterline corridor.
Wake trails coherently from the stern toward screen-left; the filled tan sail drives bow-first travel.
The mast, rigging, tan sail and established cargo remain aboard and spatially continuous.
The horizon and sky stay wide and open so the sea reads enormous around the small boat.

[Frame]
- Keen @ lower-left area; standing in the boat with knees softly braced, one hand lightly near the tiller and the other beginning to lift in anticipation; facing toward screen-right water and boat travel.
- Preserve canonical relative size, modified only by the authored depth relationship.

[Negative Space]
Lead room stays open frame-right for the approved direction of travel.
Reserve the screen-right water beside and ahead of the bow for Squeaky’s imminent surfacing and pacing corridor.
Keep open sea ahead of the bow so left-to-right travel has visible lead room.
Leave upper-frame sky and horizon uncluttered to make the empty ocean feel enormous.

[Camera]
Wide establishing lens relationship, camera at low boat-side height from the starboard side, looking slightly across the hull toward the forward screen-right travel direction. Keep mild perspective depth in the sea but avoid warping Keen or the boat. The camera is not centered on Keen as a portrait; it is staged as an ocean-scale opener with lead room ahead of the bow.

[Light]
Use the approved Scene Look for palette, ocean material, sky, cloud structure and daylight quality: bright open-water illumination with a faint dimming weight on the far horizon. Keep Keen and the sailboat cleanly readable against the water with soft daylight modelling, small specular breaks on the waves and coherent wake foam trailing behind the stern. Depth should sell enormous empty distance without fogging out the foreground action corridor.

[Performance Freedom]
Animation owns performance, movement, recovery and camera evolution.

[Protect]
Keen wears exactly two aged-gold open cuffs with blank settings, one on each wrist; no crystals, stones or glow.
Preserve the same little sailboat with tan sail, mast, rigging, open satchel, rolled blanket, folded map and small food pouch aboard.
Do not show the map in Keen’s hands in the opening frame; the map remains part of the cargo for later action.
Boat travel is bow-first left-to-right with starboard side visible; no sideways slide, stern-first motion or reversed screen direction implied.
Living performance lock: Keen, Squeaky has a specific motivated eyeline target and a readable active thought in the eyes. Use a precise asymmetric expression; no vacant forward stare, unfocused eyes, frozen smile, mannequin pose or generic camera-facing expression.

[Forbidden]
No portrait, locked extreme action pose or payoff, identity or scale drift, changed accessories, omitted reference features, duplicates, anatomy errors, extra props, text, watermark or body-mounted bags, sacks, baskets or dangling loads. Preserve the locked Scene Look.

relativeScaleAndGeography.correction: Reduce Keen and the boat to a much smaller scale against a vast open sea, and leave clear open water at screen-right for Squeaky’s future surface area.
